liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): The opening notes of Fire are called glorious and moving; Fire is a highlight, with Brent ripping [12][13]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Samson is a highlight, with Brent playing hard [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Dawn broke during the transition from Scarlet into Fire, which the reviewer found very beautiful [5]

## The recordings

- **gd82-11-26.sbd.streeter.21065.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 114 min; rated 4.11/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: This soundboard source is pristine, unlike the high-generation cassettes that circulated since the early 1980s; The muddy older cassette hid a gem; this source reveals the show's quality [7][11]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.clugston.5647.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 114 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: A tick was removed from Sugaree; Let It Grow had channel dropouts patched by copying the remaining channel, giving mono; Cuts exist in Minglewood Blues, the start of Let It Grow, and Drums [3]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.jakec.34204.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 116 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.fried-lai.1419.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 108 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Part of a three-day festival with an incongruous lineup; the venue was a rocky field and the event ran poorly and late [5]
- The Dead played last; only about 500 hardcore fans remained when they started [5]
- Bobby and the Midnites opened the next day at noon; the reviewer says that set was smoking [6]
- The band played around 5 am in a short, compact show, with energy [7]
- Road crew needed about 90 minutes, 3:00 to 4:30 am, to set up after Wailers, Toots, B-52's, Gladys Knight, Jimmy Cliff [9]
- While Phil tuned up, rastas nearby shouted impatiently at the slow-setup band, and Phil replied to them [9]
- Phil sounds like he is having fun and is pushed forward in the mix [10]
- Gladys Knight reportedly ended her set early, upset at the Heads camped out sleeping while waiting for the Dead [14]
- Calls it one of the most underrated shows of the era, possibly because of the high-generation cassettes in circulation [7]
- Notes the Compendium reviewers found no highlights, but the reviewer disagrees, finding a unique funk [10]
- Says the Compendium wrongly panned this show [12]
- Surprised by the Compendium listing no highlights; reviewer still finds lots of great playing [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd82-11-26.sbd.streeter.21065.sbeok.shnf**: source: lineage: MSC(Sony TCD-5M) > WAV > SHNrecording:MSC - master soundboard cassette w/ Dolby B by Frank Streeterdigital transfer:Nakamichi CD 2 cassette deck > HHB… [1]. Also: Transferred via Nakamichi deck to HHB 850 CD burner by Streeter and Henry Fisher, then WAV and SHN [1]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.clugston.5647.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: (uncertain) Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > DAT> CDR [3]. Also: The original transcription ran about 5% fast [3]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.jakec.34204.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jake C; source: SBD->CM->DAT [2]
- **gd1982-11-26.sbd.fried-lai.1419.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Bruce Fried; transferred by Mike Lai; source: SDB>>MR>>PCM>>DAT>>CDR [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.deadlists.com: [Grateful Dead 11/26/82 poster](http://www.deadlists.com/posters/1980s/19821126d.html) [18]
